text: Research on other ILs are limited at this time. IL-10 has been implicated as an important mediator of processes that drive myoblast proliferation and myofiber growth (171). Other evidence suggests that IL-4 is involved in myogenic differentiation (194). IL-7 also is believed to play a role in muscle hypertrophy and myogenesis (164), and IL-8 has been shown to have potent anticatabolic effects on skeletal muscle (138). Substantially more research is needed for developing a complete understanding of the roles of each of these IL isoforms (and perhaps others) with respect to exercise-induced muscular adaptations.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 1: Hypertrophy-Related Responses and Adaptations to Exercise Stress
